sentences.text: Barnesiella intestinihominis was isolated from human faeces and described as an anaerobic, non-motile, rod-shaped bacterium producing succinic and acetic acids as end products of glucose metabolism.
A study reported that in mice, recolonization with an intestinal microbiota that contains Barnesiella correlated with elimination of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus.

The same study reported that in patients undergoing allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, intestinal colonization with Barnesiella conferred resistance to intestinal domination and bloodstream infection with these enterococci.

Another study identified Barnesiella intestinihominis as one of two species involved during cyclophosphamide therapy, reporting that it accumulated in the colon and promoted infiltration of immune cells into cancer lesions.
